impact_summary: Unprecedented southwest monsoon rainfall led to widespread inundation of low-lying districts, 35 major reservoir spillway gates opened, affecting over 5 million citizens.
key_takeaways: Precipitation accumulation over 72 hours alongside saturated catchments is the critical leading indicator for catastrophic lowland flooding.
source: Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) / CWC Historical Archive

impact_summary: Severe localized cloudburst over fragile tea plantation slopes triggered catastrophic debris flows down the Iruvaazhinji river basin, flattening settlements.
key_takeaways: Steep slope geometry (>35°) coupled with antecedent 48-hour rainfall exceeding 200mm creates an immediate tipping point for pore-water pressure failure.
source: Geological Survey of India (GSI) Post-Disaster Report / IMD

impact_summary: Intense torrential monsoon precipitation led to massive slope destabilization of Muthappan hill, burying several homes under deep lateritic mud.
key_takeaways: Laterite soil profiles saturated by continuous 3-day precipitation become highly vulnerable to sudden shearing.
source: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) Case Study

impact_summary: Deep-seated rock and soil failure near Eravikulam National Park border crushed plantation quarters following persistent heavy monsoon downpours.
key_takeaways: Isolated high-altitude Western Ghats valleys require dedicated automated rainfall telemetry because radar coverage can suffer from mountain beam blockage.

impact_summary: Severe pre-monsoon dry spell coupled with desiccating katabatic winds fanned rapid surface brush fires across hundreds of acres of natural sandalwood forest.
key_takeaways: When relative humidity drops below 25% with sustained winds exceeding 30 km/h, fire propagation velocity multiplies exponentially.
source: Kerala Forest and Wildlife Department Post-Fire Audit

impact_summary: Inflow from eastern ghat rivers (Pamba, Manimala, Meenachil) coincided with high Arabian Sea tides, blocking drainage out to sea through the Thottappally spillway.
key_takeaways: Coastal lowlands below sea level have severe drainage discharge bottlenecks during tidal peaks even if rainfall has subsided.
